National Laboratory of the Rockies | 32 Secondary Frequency Control Secondary Frequency Control National Laboratory of the Rockies | 33 Secondary Frequency Control (AGC and ACE) Secondary Frequency Control (AGC and ACE) • Automatic generation control (AGC) is the automated secondary frequency response tool available to SOs Simplified illustration of AGC control using scheduled/actual frequency (green) ◦ Hold frequency at/close to nominal (50/60 Hz) and interchange schedule/actual (red) to establish ACE ◦ Maintain scheduled interchanges ◦ Maintain unit generation optimally (system-wide). • AGC operates on a control signal called the area control error (ACE) for a control area and is a linear combination of: ◦ Deviation of frequency ◦ Deviation of tie-line flows. • ACE is distributed to resources through: ◦ Participation factors (splitting ACE signal to generators on AGC) ◦ “Raise/lower” pulses (~4 seconds). NOTE: AGC is a complex multifaceted topic we will not delve further into today. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 34 Control Strategies: Tertiary Frequency Control Control Strategies: Tertiary Frequency Control Tertiary Frequency Control Tertiary Frequency Control • Quantity ◦ Required to restore primary and secondary response and to restore interconnectors back to scheduled values following large mismatches ◦ Typically manual response via SO instruction (sometimes automatic via under-frequency starting) ◦ Either quick start-up or quick ramp-up ◦ Longer time and thus not necessarily required to be synchronized ◦ Worst single contingency on own interconnected system. • Future ◦ With larger units or additional interconnectors carrying larger amounts of power, these may replace Kapichira as the largest unit contingency. • Activation and activation time ◦ Start-up times of existing thermal units and hydro units ◦ Slow and thus communications with thermal plants specifically to ascertain accurate start-up and synchronize times as well as ramp-rates to provide tertiary response should be verified.
